name: control_branch
motivation: Round 24 (single-cluster loop): ncu warp-stall sampling at 32-cycle period on cutlass_stream_k_splitk_01 puts 13.4 % of all samples on BRA PCs (+2.1 % on the BPT.TRAP fall-through of asserted branches, reason branch_resolving) against 0.8 % of the engine's issue gaps; cutlass_fp8_dense_08 7-8 %. Both trees charge a BRA 1 cycle (structural) and the predecessors' control.turnover was a placeholder, so the warp-PC redirect / predicate resolution of a branch has never been measured. The engine already has the application path: an instance bound to an instance_timing program with event control_transition pushes WarpState::control_floor (used by control.reconvergence for BSSY).
engine_rule_declared_before_data: control.branch binds every BRA instance; its control_envelope(branch_taken) is a floor on the warp's next issue after the BRA (control_floor, existing rule). branch_taken is a converter axis = 1 when the warp's next dynamic instance is not at pc + 16 (16 B SASS), else 0 (last instance of a warp: 0). The leaf excludes instruction fetch of the target: the probe window is L0-resident by construction, and a cold target line keeps being charged by instruction.fetch.
probe: tools/microbench/control_branch/probe/branch.cu, one CTA, W warps in {1, 4} (W = 4 puts one warp per SMSP), timing thread warp 0 lane 0, t_s / t_w clock64 around a window of U units, U in {16, 32, 64, 128}, straight-line (no loop) unless stated. Predicates p (true) and q (false) come from a kernel argument read once before t_s (opaque to the compiler). Unit variants: taken: `@p bra NEXT; <skipped block = one fence.gpu (MEMBAR) that the taken branch jumps over>; NEXT: FFMA chain step` (predicated-taken forward branch over 16 B, predicate ready long before); nottaken: `@q bra LOCAL_k` with the same body (predicated, falls through; every unit has its own local target block so ptxas cannot merge the branches); uncond: `bra NEXT` without predicate (the gate requires the BRA to survive ptxas; a folded variant is unrealised); taken_dep: `setp` producing p from the chain value immediately before `@p bra NEXT` (predicate dependency on the critical path); loop: a counted loop whose trip count is read from a kernel argument (U, not a compile-time constant, so it is not unrolled), body = one FFMA chain step + counter update; back edge taken U-1 times; the loop entry / exit checks (constant count) are listed. The FFMA chain step is `d = fma(d, a, b)` on one register so the body cost is the installed FFMA result latency per unit. --launches 16 --reps 257, two runs (run-a, run-b) in one job per device. Predicates use bra (not bra.uni) so the branch is a per-thread predicated BRA as in the corpus.
sass_gate: Let the window be the SASS between t_s and t_w. Instructions are classified as scaling (count proportional to U) or constant (count independent of U, verified by comparing the U = 16 and U = 128 kernels of the same variant). Scaling set must be exactly: BRA x U (loop: the back-edge BRA executes U-1 times; static count 1) and the chain FFMA x U; for taken / uncond also the skipped MEMBAR x U. Constant set may contain BSSY / BSSY.RECONVERGENT / BSYNC / loop entry-exit BRA / ISETP / predicate materialisation, each listed in model.json; any other scaling instruction (e.g. a re-materialised predicate per unit, spills, LDC inside the window) fails the kernel -> unrealised. The whole window must fit 16 KiB. An uncond variant whose BRA is folded by ptxas is unrealised (expected).

derivation.E(variant, W, U): mean over samples of t_w - t_s
derivation.slope(variant, W): OLS slope of E over U in {16, 32, 64, 128} (cycles per unit)
derivation.body(variant): installed FFMA result_latency_cycles of the device (dependent chain step) + the issue cost of the unit's other scaling non-branch instructions summed from the SASS control words (sass_ctrl.py o_s convention); constant-set instructions enter the intercept only and are not subtracted
derivation.install values: control_envelope(branch_taken = 1) = branch(taken, W = 1); control_envelope(branch_taken = 0) = branch(nottaken, W = 1); uncond, taken_dep, loop and the W = 4 cells are reported (uncond vs taken = predicate cost, taken_dep - taken = predicate resolution on the critical path, loop vs taken = back-edge vs forward)

acceptance.cell: max relative fit residual <= 2 % and run agreement <= 3 % (or <= 1 cycle) -> measured; <= 5 % / <= 8 % -> experimental and listed; else unrealised
acceptance.negative: a negative branch() within 2 se of 0 installs 0; beyond -> reported, not installed
acceptance.both devices: each device installs its own values; no cross-device fill

install: common/mechanisms/control.branch.json (program event control_transition, operation_classes [BRA], parameter_schema instance_timing, field_models control_envelope discrete over branch_taken); common/axes.json gains branch_taken (converter axis, both builders); <arch>/leaves/control.branch.json with the two points; sources control_branch.<device>.<run>. tree build && tree validate --strict must pass; one two-architecture 500 A/B round; version-1 runs (r1) stay on disk as the record of the failed gate.
not_allowed: no case-cycle tuning; no values from other machines; no threshold or derivation change after data; BRX / JMP / CALL / RET / EXIT are out of scope (reported if they appear in the census).
supersedes: tools/microbench/control_branch/protocol.json (version 1; its only runs h100-r1 / b300-r1 are recorded as not installable: every kernel fails the version-1 SASS gate for structural reasons listed below, so all cells are unrealised under version 1)
why_version_2: Version 1's gate asked for a window with no BSSY / BSYNC and with a dead FFMA inside every skipped block. On both targets ptxas (a) emits one or two BSSY / BSSY.RECONVERGENT per kernel for the predicated forward-jump region (a per-window constant, not scaling with U), (b) dead-code-eliminates the dead FFMA even behind fence.gpu, (c) merges identical not-taken branches unless each has a local target, (d) folds the unconditional bra. These are properties of the compiler, not of the measurement; the version-1 data (slopes identical across runs, linear in U) are therefore reported but not installed. Version 2 restates the gate in terms of what scales with U and freezes the realised unit forms before the version-2 runs (h100-r2 / b300-r2).
